definition: Watchkeeping means maintaining an assigned lookout or operational watch and handing over relevant information when relieved.
example: A ship’s watch officer records nearby traffic and passes the situation to the next officer.
sense_note: The label can also refer to watches outside maritime work.

definition: watchOS is Apple’s operating system for Apple Watch devices.
example: A developer tests how a workout display behaves on a watch.

definition: Watcom SQL was a relational database product that preceded the SQL Anywhere line.
example: A database specialist checks old Watcom SQL scripts before migrating a legacy application.

definition: Water-based pipe coating uses a coating carried primarily in water to protect or finish a pipe surface.
example: A technician evaluates adhesion on a coated pipe sample.

definition: Water quality modelling uses mathematical or computational models to estimate how physical, chemical or biological conditions affect water quality.
example: A watershed team compares modeled nutrient levels under different runoff scenarios.

definition: Web crawling automatically discovers and retrieves accessible web pages, often by following links.
example: A documentation team crawls its own website to find broken links.

definition: Web development creates and maintains websites and browser-based applications.
example: A developer builds a contact form and verifies that it works on mobile devices.

definition: Web filtering controls which web requests or content users may access according to a policy.
example: A school network blocks access to sites in categories disallowed by its policy.

definition: WebCT was a learning management system for delivering and administering online courses.
example: An instructor posts course readings and reviews assignment submissions in a legacy WebCT course.

definition: WebCTRL is a building automation platform for monitoring and controlling building equipment and conditions.
example: An operator reviews ventilation alarms from several buildings in a common interface.

definition: WebDriver is a standardized interface for controlling browser behavior programmatically, commonly for automated testing.
example: A test opens a page, clicks a button and checks the displayed confirmation.

definition: WebDriverJS refers to JavaScript tooling for driving browsers through WebDriver, particularly Selenium’s JavaScript bindings.
example: A tester writes a JavaScript check that verifies a modal can be closed.
sense_note: The label has also been used for other JavaScript WebDriver clients.

definition: Website optimization improves measured website performance or outcomes by diagnosing issues and testing changes.
example: A team compresses large images to reduce page load time.
sense_note: The goal may be speed, accessibility, conversion or another measurable outcome.

definition: Website wireframing sketches the structure, layout and navigation of a website before detailed design or implementation.
example: A designer maps the search results and filtering controls in a low-fidelity layout.

definition: WebVR was an experimental browser API for accessing virtual reality devices and presenting virtual environments from web pages.
example: An archivist examines a legacy browser demo that used WebVR to display a scene in a headset.

definition: Weed control manages unwanted plants to reduce harm to crops, landscapes or ecosystems.
example: A gardener uses mulch to reduce weed establishment in a planting bed.

definition: WhatsApp is a messaging service that supports text, media and voice or video calls.
example: A volunteer team uses a WhatsApp group to coordinate an event.

definition: Wi-Fi 6 is the Wi-Fi generation based on IEEE 802.11ax, which improves efficiency and capacity in busy wireless networks.
example: A campus equips a crowded classroom with Wi-Fi 6 access points for many simultaneous devices.

definition: Wi-Fi Direct lets compatible devices establish a direct Wi-Fi connection without joining an existing access point.
example: A phone sends a document to a nearby compatible printer without joining the office network.

definition: Wi-Fi test engineering designs and runs tests for wireless behavior, compliance and interoperability.
example: An engineer measures how well a device maintains connectivity while moving between access points.

definition: Wildlife observation records animal presence, behavior or habitat use through attentive field observation.
example: A naturalist logs the time, habitat and behavior of birds seen along a survey route.

definition: Will and testament preparation documents a person’s directions for administering and distributing their estate after death.
example: A legal professional records a client's instructions about beneficiaries and an executor.

definition: Windows 10 is a Microsoft desktop operating system released after Windows 8.1 and before Windows 11.
example: A technician checks whether a driver supports the installed Windows 10 edition.

definition: Windows 7 is a Microsoft desktop operating system that succeeded Windows Vista.
example: An archivist sets up Windows 7 to inspect the behavior of a legacy application.

definition: Windows 8 is a Microsoft desktop operating system that introduced a touch-oriented Start screen alongside the desktop.
example: A support specialist helps a user switch between the Start screen and a desktop program.

definition: Windows Meeting Space was a Windows Vista application for local collaboration, sharing and presentation.
example: A user shares a presentation with participants in a legacy Windows Vista session.

definition: Windows Performance Analyzer examines recorded Windows performance traces using graphs and tables.
example: An engineer inspects a trace to see whether CPU or disk activity coincides with a slow launch.

definition: Windows Performance Recorder collects tracing data about Windows system and application activity.
example: A developer records a trace during an unusually slow program startup.

definition: Windows Performance Toolkit is a Microsoft collection of tools for recording and analyzing Windows performance data.
example: A team captures a startup trace with Windows Performance Recorder and analyzes it with Windows Performance Analyzer.

definition: Windows software development creates and maintains software intended to run on Microsoft Windows.
example: A developer builds and tests a desktop application against supported Windows versions.

definition: The Windows software trace preprocessor helps instrument source code for collecting diagnostic trace messages on Windows.
example: A driver developer adds trace statements to distinguish startup events during troubleshooting.

definition: Windows support diagnoses and resolves issues encountered by users or systems running Windows.
example: A technician investigates why a user’s application no longer starts after an update.

definition: Windows systems administration configures, maintains and monitors Windows-based computers and services.
example: An administrator applies approved settings consistently to a group of managed workstations.

definition: Windows Vista is a Microsoft desktop operating system released between Windows XP and Windows 7.
example: A compatibility specialist checks how a legacy installer behaves on Windows Vista.

definition: Windows XP Media Center Edition was an edition of Windows XP designed for media playback and related home-entertainment functions.
example: A user browses recorded television in a legacy Media Center setup.

definition: Windows XP Professional x64 Edition was Microsoft’s 64-bit x86-compatible edition of Windows XP Professional.
example: A technician checks whether an older workstation has compatible 64-bit drivers.

definition: Winemaking is the production of wine through fermentation and related preparation, maturation and finishing steps.
example: A producer compares how different maturation vessels influence a wine’s character.

definition: WinJS is a JavaScript library that supplies controls and utilities for building user interfaces, originally for Windows apps.
example: A maintainer reviews a legacy app’s WinJS list control before replacing its interface.

definition: WKWebView is Apple’s embeddable WebKit view for displaying web content in an application.
example: A developer displays an HTML help page inside an iOS app.

definition: The Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act is a U.S. law that requires qualifying health coverage offering mastectomy benefits to cover specified related care.
example: A benefits specialist reviews plan materials for required post-mastectomy reconstruction coverage.
